blocks.text: Design a distributed locking service, the kind of system behind Zookeeper or a Redis-based Redlock, that guarantees only one process across an entire distributed system can hold a given lock at a time, protecting a shared resource from concurrent, conflicting access. The famous, genuinely hard problem here is not acquiring a lock, it is what happens when a lock holder pauses for an unusually long time, a garbage collection pause or a network partition, has its lock automatically expire and handed to someone else, and then wakes up still believing it safely holds it. Solving this correctly, without simply hoping pauses never happen, is what this design is actually about.

Solving this correctly, without simply hoping pauses never happen, is what this design is actually about.

blocks.alt: A lock grant issues a strictly increasing fencing token, and the protected resource itself rejects any write whose token is not higher than the highest one it has already accepted

blocks.text: The technique that solves this is fencing tokens, every successful lock acquisition returns a token strictly greater than any issued before it, and the protected resource, not the lock service, is the one that actually enforces safety, refusing any write carrying a token lower than the highest one it has already seen, regardless of whether the client sending it still believes it holds the lock.

blocks.text: A client should be able to acquire an exclusive lock on a named resource, receiving a fencing token on success. A lock should automatically expire after a configured time-to-live if its holder never releases or renews it, preventing a crashed client from blocking everyone else forever. A protected resource should reject any write carrying a token lower than the highest one it has already accepted. A client should be able to explicitly release a lock it holds before its natural expiry.

blocks.alt: True mutual exclusion across machines, safety even when a lock holder pauses or crashes, never deadlocking on a dead client, low latency acquire and release, and tokens trusted only from the real lock service

blocks.text: True mutual exclusion across machines means only one process across the entire distributed system should ever hold a given lock at once, not merely within one machine or process. Safety even when a lock holder pauses means a client that pauses past its lock's expiry must never be allowed to corrupt shared state later, once it eventually wakes up still believing it holds the lock. Never deadlocking on a dead client means a crashed holder's lock has to expire and become available again, rather than blocking every other client indefinitely. Low latency acquire and release means using this service on a real, busy critical section has to stay fast. And tokens trusted only from the real lock service means a fencing token only means anything if it genuinely, verifiably came from the lock service itself, not something a client fabricated.
blocks.content: True mutual exclusion across machines means only one process across the entire distributed system should ever hold a given lock at once, not merely within one machine or process. Safety even when a lock holder pauses means a client that pauses past its lock's expiry must never be allowed to corrupt shared state later, once it eventually wakes up still believing it holds the lock. Never deadlocking on a dead client means a crashed holder's lock has to expire and become available again, rather than blocking every other client indefinitely. Low latency acquire and release means using this service on a real, busy critical section has to stay fast. And tokens trusted only from the real lock service means a fencing token only means anything if it genuinely, verifiably came from the lock service itself, not something a client fabricated.

blocks.text: This design assumes the lock service itself runs as a small, consensus-based cluster, so its own failure does not mean losing track of every current lock's true owner and token. Fencing tokens are assumed strictly increasing and globally unique across the entire lock service, never reused, even across different resources. Enforcing the fencing token check is assumed to be the protected resource's own responsibility, the lock service issues correct, trustworthy tokens, but cannot itself force a resource to actually check them.

blocks.text: A platform at real scale might see tens of thousands of lock acquire and release operations per second across an enormous number of distinct, independently lockable resources. Acquiring or releasing a lock is expected to complete in a few milliseconds, fast enough to genuinely protect a real, busy critical section without becoming its own bottleneck. Given real-world operating conditions, a meaningful fraction of clients will genuinely pause, due to garbage collection or a network partition, or crash outright, while holding a lock at some point, which is exactly the ordinary condition this design has to handle safely, not an exotic edge case.

class LockGrant:
    # The result of a lock acquisition attempt: whether it succeeded, and, if
    # so, the strictly increasing fencing token issued for this grant.
    def __init__(self, granted, token):
        self.granted = granted
        self.token = token


class LockState:
    # One resource's current lock state: who holds it, its fencing token, and
    # when it expires.
    def __init__(self, owner_client_id, token, expires_at):
        self.owner_client_id = owner_client_id
        self.token = token
        self.expires_at = expires_at


class LockService:
    # Grants exclusive locks with strictly increasing fencing tokens; a lock
    # past its expiry is treated as free and can be granted to a new client
    # with a genuinely higher token than any issued before.
    def __init__(self):
        self.locks = {}
        self.next_token = 1

    def acquire(self, resource_id, client_id, now, ttl_millis):
        existing = self.locks.get(resource_id)
        if existing is not None and existing.expires_at > now:
            return LockGrant(False, -1)  # still held by someone else, not yet expired
        token = self.next_token
        self.next_token += 1  # always strictly greater than any token issued before
        self.locks[resource_id] = LockState(client_id, token, now + ttl_millis)
        return LockGrant(True, token)


class ProtectedResource:
    # A resource protected by fencing tokens: it independently rejects any
    # write whose token is not higher than the highest one it has already
    # accepted, regardless of what the lock service or the writing client believes.
    def __init__(self):
        self.highest_token_seen = 0
        self.data = ""

    def apply_write(self, token, new_data):
        if token <= self.highest_token_seen:
            return False  # stale token: this client no longer safely holds the lock
        self.highest_token_seen = token
        self.data = new_data
        return True

    def current_data(self):
        return self.data


def main():
    lock_service = LockService()
    resource = ProtectedResource()

    # Client A acquires the lock at time 0, with a 1000ms time-to-live.
    grant_a = lock_service.acquire("resource-1", "client-A", 0, 1000)
    print(f"Client A acquires lock: granted={grant_a.granted} token={grant_a.token}")

    # Client A "pauses" (a long GC pause or network partition) and never renews or releases.
    # Time passes well beyond the lock's 1000ms TTL.

    # Client B acquires the lock at time 1500, since A's lock has already expired.
    grant_b = lock_service.acquire("resource-1", "client-B", 1500, 1000)
    print(f"Client B acquires lock after A's expired: granted={grant_b.granted} token={grant_b.token}")

    # Client B writes using its genuinely current, higher token.
    b_write_accepted = resource.apply_write(grant_b.token, "B's update")
    print("Client B's write accepted:", b_write_accepted)

    # Client A finally wakes up, still believing it holds token 1, and tries to write.
    a_write_accepted = resource.apply_write(grant_a.token, "A's stale update")
    print("Client A's stale write accepted (should be false):", a_write_accepted)

    print("Resource's final data (should only reflect B's write):", resource.current_data())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Consistency: strongly consistent lock ownership at the lock service, paired with a fast, purely local token comparison at the protected resource.
